gloss: with effort, at great pains, long-awaited

definitions.explanation: Indicating that something required considerable effort or trouble; often implying the effort may be wasted.
Going out of one's way to do something; taking special trouble.
A rare or precious opportunity that shouldn't be wasted.

examples.japanese: {折角|せっかく}{来|き}たのに{休|やす}みだった。
examples.english: I came all this way but it was closed.

examples.japanese: {折角|せっかく}{作|つく}った{料理|りょうり}が{冷|さ}めてしまった。
examples.english: The food I took the trouble to make has gotten cold.

examples.japanese: {折角|せっかく}{買|か}ったのに、{一度|いちど}も{使|つか}わなかった。
examples.english: I went to the trouble of buying it, but never used it even once.

examples.japanese: {折角|せっかく}{来|き}てくれたんだから、ゆっくりしていってね。
examples.english: Since you came all this way, please take your time and relax.

examples.japanese: {折角|せっかく}ですから、いただきます。
examples.english: Since you've gone to the trouble, I'll have some.

examples.japanese: {折角|せっかく}{京都|きょうと}に{来|き}たのだから、{神社|じんじゃ}を{見|み}に{行|い}こう。
examples.english: Since we've come all the way to Kyoto, let's go see a shrine.

examples.japanese: {折角|せっかく}のチャンスだ。
{折角|せっかく}の{休|やす}みだから{出|で}かけよう。
examples.english: Since it's a precious day off, let's go out.

examples.japanese: {折角|せっかく}の{機会|きかい}なので、ぜひ{参加|さんか}してください。
examples.english: Since it's such a rare opportunity, please do participate.

notes:
{折角|せっかく} expresses that effort has been made or an opportunity is special/rare. It often appears in two patterns:

1. EXPRESSING WASTED EFFORT:
{折角|せっかく}〜のに (despite taking the trouble to...)
Implies disappointment when effort doesn't pay off.

2. EXPRESSING RARE OPPORTUNITY:
{折角|せっかく}の〜だから (since it's such a rare ~)
Encourages making the most of a special chance.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {折角|せっかく}〜のに: even though I/you took the trouble to...
- {折角|せっかく}の{機会|きかい}: rare opportunity
- {折角|せっかく}ですから: since you've gone to the trouble (polite acceptance)
